newsitem.title: UK: Granada shares slip with retreating market.
newsitem.headline: Granada shares slip with retreating market.

text.p: Shares in Granada Group Plc eased with a declining market on Wednesday after showing little initial reaction to first-half profits at the top end of analysts' expectations.
After creeping up a penny in the wake of the results, the shares retreated to 897, down 5-1/2p, by 0940 GMT.
"The numbers were reasonably good but we didn't see a huge dividend and they had a good run up over the last week ahead of the results," one market-maker said.

Pre-tax profit before one-off items rose 33 percent to 243 million stg, compared with a analysts expectations in a range between 235 million stg and 240 million. The interim dividend was raised 10 percent to 4.66p.
Analysts said the results looked better than expected but added that the market would be looking for further comment on Granada's continuing disposal programme and its underlying performance.
"Profits are at the top end of expectations but the dividend looks at the low end, though that's probably understandable given their high debt levels," said one analyst.
The analyst noted a strong performance in Granada's hotels businesses, with yield for instance up 16 percent.
"Hotels look to be having a storming time, with yield and occupancy rates very good...it suggests they bought Forte at a good time."

Chairman Gerry Robinson said all four of Granada's divisions had performed strongly. "We will continue to grow these businesses organically and maximise the benefit of the tremendous assets that the company now has."
Chief executive Charles Allen added that the "first few weeks of the second half are showing an encouraging start to trading".
